theory.intro: On a **reducing balance loan** the interest each period is charged on the amount still owing, not on the amount first borrowed. Each repayment lowers the balance, so the next interest charge is smaller.
facts: Each row of a loan table gives closing balance $= P + I - R$, for opening balance $P$, interest $I$ and repayment $R$.
The interest is always charged on the **opening** balance, and the repayment is taken off afterwards.
The rate per period must match the repayment period: $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly gives $\dfrac{0.072}{12} = 0.006$ per month.
Each month's interest is rounded to the nearest cent before the closing balance is worked out.
One row's closing balance becomes the next row's opening balance.
The total repaid is the repayment multiplied by the number of periods, and the total interest is that total minus the amount borrowed.
A graph of the balance owing falls slowly at first and then more steeply, because early repayments are mostly interest.
If the interest charged in a period is more than the repayment, the balance grows and the loan is never repaid.
steps: Work out the interest rate per period.
Multiply the opening balance by that rate to get the interest.
Add the interest and subtract the repayment to get the closing balance.
Carry the closing balance down as the next opening balance.

foundation.question_text:
A reducing balance loan of $\$8000$ is charged interest at $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$250$.
Find the interest charged in the first month and the balance owing at the end of that month.

A reducing balance loan of $\$15\,000$ is charged interest at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$450$.
Find the balance owing at the end of the first month.

A reducing balance loan of $\$5000$ is charged interest at $18\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$300$.
Find the balance owing at the end of the **second** month, rounding each month's interest to the nearest cent.

A reducing balance loan of $\$12\,000$ is charged interest at $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$400$.
Find the balance owing at the end of the **third** month, rounding each month's interest to the nearest cent.

Nadia owes $\$6200$ on a reducing balance loan charged at $24\%$ p.a. compounded monthly and repays $\$120$ each month.
Show that this loan will never be repaid, and find the balance at the end of the first month.
foundation.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.24}{12} = 0.02$
$I = 6200 \times 0.02$
$= \$124$
The interest of $\$124$ is more than the repayment of $\$120$, so the balance rises.
Balance $= 6200 + 124 - 120$
$= \$6204$

foundation.question_text:
A reducing balance loan of $\$18\,000$ is repaid by monthly repayments of $\$395$ over $5$ years.
Find the total amount repaid and the total interest charged.
foundation.solution_text:
Number of repayments $= 5 \times 12 = 60$
Total repaid $= 395 \times 60$
$= \$23\,700$
Total interest $= 23\,700 - 18\,000$
$= \$5700$

The curve starts at $\$200\,000$, so that is the amount borrowed.
At $200$ months the curve is level with the $\$100\,000$ gridline.
About $\$100\,000$ is still owing after $200$ months.

development.question_text:
The first two months of a reducing balance loan of $\$60\,000$ at $6.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$700$, are shown below.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \textbf{Month} & \textbf{Opening } (P) & \textbf{Interest } (I) & \textbf{Repayment } (R) & \textbf{Closing } (P+I-R) \\ \hline 1 & \$60\,000 & \$330 & \$700 & \$59\,630 \\ \hline 2 & \$59\,630 & A & \$700 & B \\ \hline \end{array}$
Find the values of $A$ and $B$, to the nearest cent.

A reducing balance loan of $\$9000$ is charged interest at $10.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$500$.
Of the $\$1500$ repaid over the first three months, how much was interest and how much reduced the principal?
Round each month's interest to the nearest cent.

A reducing balance loan of $\$30\,000$ is charged interest at $8\%$ p.a. compounded **quarterly**, with quarterly repayments of $\$1500$.
Find the balance owing at the end of the second quarter.

A reducing balance home loan of $\$310\,000$ is repaid by monthly repayments of $\$2140$ over $30$ years.
Find the total interest charged.
development.solution_text:
Number of repayments $= 30 \times 12 = 360$
Total repaid $= 2140 \times 360$
$= \$770\,400$
Total interest $= 770\,400 - 310\,000$
$= \$460\,400$

development.question_text:
A reducing balance loan is charged interest at $1.5\%$ per month.
In one month the opening balance is $\$4200$ and the closing balance is $\$4113$.
Find the repayment made that month.

A personal loan of $\$4500$ is charged interest at $21.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly and the borrower repays $\$75$ each month.
Find the balance owing at the end of the second month and explain what is happening to the debt.
development.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.216}{12} = 0.018$
Month $1$: $I = 4500 \times 0.018 = \$81$, balance $= 4500 + 81 - 75 = \$4506$
Month $2$: $I = 4506 \times 0.018 = \$81.11$, balance $= 4506 + 81.11 - 75 = \$4512.11$
Each month's interest is more than the $\$75$ repayment, so the balance is growing and the loan is never repaid.

mastery.question_text:
A reducing balance loan of $\$10\,000$ is charged interest at $15\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$900$.
Build the table for the first four months and find the total interest charged over those four months.
Round each month's interest to the nearest cent.

The first month of a reducing balance loan shows an opening balance of $\$250\,000$, interest of $\$1500$, a repayment of $\$1900$ and a closing balance of $\$249\,600$.
Find the annual interest rate (compounded monthly) and the closing balance at the end of the second month.

A borrower owes $\$9600$ on a reducing balance loan charged at $13.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
What is the smallest whole-dollar monthly repayment that will actually reduce the balance owing?
mastery.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.132}{12} = 0.011$
$I = 9600 \times 0.011$
$= \$105.60$
The repayment must be more than $\$105.60$, so the smallest whole-dollar repayment is $\$106$.
